page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 32 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features a shared CPU allocation model under the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Graphics processing is driven by three NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 144 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage, and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier (top 10%) for single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, as well as Geekbench single-core execution. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform exceptionally well, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression reaching the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is strong, ranking in the top 25% for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read and write operations. Database operations, measured via Passmark and Redis SET operations, also achieve top-tier status, processing 128.07 million operations per second. Ray tracing performance on Geekbench represents a relative bottleneck, scoring in the average tier (middle 50%).

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a high-density hardware profile combining substantial GPU memory with a large system RAM footprint, though the shared CPU allocation model presents a potential performance tradeoff under sustained, non-GPU CPU-bound workloads. The lack of local storage requires external storage integration, which may impact sequential I/O-heavy tasks. This configuration is engineered for GPU-accelerated workloads, large-scale data processing, parallelized simulations, and memory-intensive database operations.
